summary: Kole Jain explains how a designer with no clients can still build a portfolio by making realistic fake projects. The process is: get a unique prompt from a site such as Good Brief or Sharpen Design, make sure it fits the niche you want to work in, expand it into a full brief with ChatGPT, collect inspiration, then design with the brief in mind and no placeholder text. He compares where to show the work (Dribbble, Behance, Notion sites, a personal website) and says how many projects are enough. For someone building a design system this is mostly career advice, but the steps of starting from a written brief and using realistic content instead of lorem ipsum carry over to any design work [inferred].
key_ideas: Without client work, a portfolio can be built from fake projects.
A good fake project starts with a good idea; get a unique prompt from a site such as Good Brief or Sharpen Design.
Pick project ideas that match the niche you want to end up working in.
Making work for everyone targets no one; without a niche you are the expert of everything and therefore nothing.
Choose a niche by what you are passionate about and whether products could reasonably be sold in it.
Turn the prompt into a full project brief (the video uses ChatGPT) and keep it in mind while designing.
Gather inspiration from Dribbble, Pinterest, Instagram or Behance before designing.
Make the design as realistic as possible, with no lorem ipsum.

Dribbble suits interfaces and Behance suits case studies; a personal website seems much more professional but costs a lot of time and energy; Notion sites are quick to set up and can be more personal than Dribbble or Behance.
Two to three case studies, or three to four interface-only projects, are enough; focus on very high-quality work that shows off your skills.

rules.rule: When you have no client work, fill the portfolio with self-initiated (fake) projects.
rules.why: A designer who has not worked with any clients otherwise has nothing to put in the portfolio.

rules.rule: Start a practice or portfolio project from a unique prompt taken from a site such as Good Brief or Sharpen Design.
rules.why: A good fake project always starts with a good idea.
rules.evidence: Head over to Good Brief or Sharpen Design to get yourself a unique prompt

rules.rule: Choose project ideas that line up with the niche you want to end up working in.

rules.rule: Write a full project brief before designing, keep it in mind throughout, and make the design as realistic as possible.

rules.rule: Gather inspiration (for example from Dribbble, Pinterest, Instagram or Behance) before starting the design.

rules.rule: Do not use lorem ipsum; fill designs with realistic content.

rules.rule: Focus on making very high-quality work for the portfolio.
